If nature contains a boson with a mass of order $10^{-12}\,$eV, $\textit{mere vacuum fluctuations}$ will lead to its efficient production around spinning stellar mass black holes, forming a gravitational atom that both drains the black hole spin and decays to produce near-monochromatic gravitational waves. Existing superradiance constraints derive primarily from spin measurements of a handful of identified black holes. Here we instead present a detailed study of the population level effect: gravitational waves arising from both the 100 million black holes in the Milky Way and the stochastic signal from axion clouds throughout the universe. We study the impact of a broad range of systematic uncertainties on the black hole properties and compute the projected axion sensitivity for LIGO, as well as the future instruments Einstein Telescope, Cosmic Explorer, and a high-frequency Magnetic Weber Bar. We demonstrate that LIGO can robustly probe axion masses from roughly $10^{-13}\,$eV to $4 \times 10^{-12}\,$eV. If the black hole population extends to masses slightly below $5\,M_{\odot}$ - as hinted for by LIGO inspiral observations - LIGO would approach $10^{-11}\,$eV. Under that same assumption we show that a future high-frequency detector could push considerably higher, potentially beyond $10^{-10}\,$eV in the most optimistic scenarios, reaching towards the lowest masses within the projected sensitivity of axion dark matter searches.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian A. R. Ellis, Orion Ning, Nicholas L. Rodd, Jan Sch\"utte-Engel

item.title: Next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order QCD corrections to photon-pair production
item.description: arXiv:2604.12613v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The production of two isolated photons at the Large Hadron Collider has applications in Higgs-boson phenomenology and in new-physics searches. In fact, measurements would provide more insight if a percent-level theoretical prediction were available. We account for next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order strong-interaction effects in the cross section for the first time. This is not only necessary to demonstrate the convergence of perturbation theory, but also results in a reduction of the theoretical uncertainty by a factor of three down to 3\%. With this, we pave the way to improved analyses.
item.dc:creator: Michal Czakon, Felix Eschment, Terry Generet, Rene Poncelet

item.title: Charmonium production at SPS and FAIR energies
item.description: arXiv:2605.29479v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this study we apply the Remler formalism to charmonium production at SPS and GSI/FAIR energies in order to investigate the effects of baryon-rich matter on charmonium production and dissociation in heavy-ion collisions within the Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD). As a first step the Remler formalism is tested in p+p collisions and then applied to p+A collisions in order to extract the nuclear absorption cross section of charmonium, which is then utilized in heavy-ion collisions. We find that the Remler formalism successfully describes charmonium production in heavy-ion collisions at SPS energies when an in-medium heavy quark potential is implemented, in which $J/\psi$ dissociates near $T_c$. Finally the same formalism is applied to the low CERN/SPS energy and GSI/FAIR energies, where we estimate charmonium production.
item.dc:creator: Taesoo Song, Jiaxing Zhao, Joerg Aichelin, Elena Bratkovskaya

item.title: Probing the Moderate-to-Large-$x$ Gluon Helicity with $J/\psi$ Production at $\sqrt{s}=\mathrm{GeV}$
item.description: arXiv:2605.30945v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the longitudinal double-spin asymmetry, $A_{LL}$, for color-singlet $J/\psi$ production in longitudinally polarized $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}\simeq27~\mathrm{GeV}$, relevant to the Spin Physics Detector at NICA. At these energies, gluon fusion probes moderate-to-large gluon momentum fractions, particularly at forward rapidity. We consider the leading-order color-singlet subprocess $gg\to J/\psi+g$ within nonrelativistic QCD and calculate polarized and unpolarized cross sections using analytic partonic hard-scattering coefficients. The color-singlet long-distance matrix element cancels in $A_{LL}$ at this order. We study the transverse-momentum and rapidity dependence of the asymmetry using different polarized and unpolarized PDF combinations, including LO and NLO PDF inputs, while keeping the hard-scattering calculation at LO. Factorization- and renormalization-scale variations are examined, and PDF and scale uncertainties are combined. The asymmetry is positive and increases with transverse momentum in the kinematically stable region. Its magnitude and uncertainty become more sensitive to the polarized gluon distribution at moderate and large $x$, with substantial differences among PDF combinations at moderate and large transverse momentum. NLO PDF uncertainties are generally smaller than LO uncertainties in central regions, but this reduction is not uniform; PDF and scale uncertainties can both become sizable at high transverse momentum and forward rapidity. Differential measurements of $A_{LL}$ at SPD could therefore provide complementary constraints on gluon helicity in a relatively unexplored kinematic region. A complete NLO hard-scattering calculation is needed for precision predictions and a quantitative assessment of higher-order effects.
item.dc:creator: Shubham Sharma, Alexey Aparin, Satyajit Puhan, Narinder Kumar, Harleen Dahiya

item.title: Core Composition Effects on the QCD Axion Mass Limit from Neutron Star Cooling
item.description: arXiv:2606.07742v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Neutron stars are very dense media in which axions may be produced. This has been used to set a limit on the QCD axion mass, usually under the assumption that only neutrons, protons, electrons, and muons appear in the star core. Given the extreme conditions reached within neutron stars, it is reasonable to consider that other particles, such as hyperons and $\Delta$ resonances, may appear in the neutron star core. In this work, we study how the limit on the mass of QCD axions, namely KSVZ and DFSZ invisible axions, is altered when different equations of state are used, allowing for heavier particles to appear in the neutron star core. We find that this dependence is in general mild and thus reinforces the reliability of the known limit. Additionally, in the DFSZ scenario, it may drive the limit within the sensitivity window for IAXO. This would allow this experiment to discern the composition of neutron star cores if an axion were to be observed within that window.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Arias-Arag\'on, Federico Nola

item.title: Hadronisation of in-medium $c\bar c$ pairs to the exotic $X(3872)$
item.description: arXiv:2606.23261v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The production ratios of hidden-charm hadrons observed in nuclear collisions reflect the degree of separation that the precursor $c\bar c$ pair develops inside the quark-gluon plasma. The respective hadronisation amplitude manifests this relation through the position-space inner products of the in-medium and in-vacuum $c\bar c$ wave functions. The exotic $X(3872)$, whose structure accommodates a dominant loosely bound molecular component together with a smaller compact component, stands as a novel hard probe of this spatial dependence. In this Letter, relative production measurements of $J/\psi$, $\psi(2S)$ and $X(3872)$ hadrons performed by the LHC collaborations are understood through the spatial dispersion of in-medium charm anti-charm systems.
item.dc:creator: Henrique Legoinha, Bernardo Pic\~ao, Pedro Bicudo

item.title: axionbloch: an Open-Source Python Package for Simulating Axion-Induced Spin Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2606.23749v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The interaction of ultralight bosonic dark matter with spins can be interpreted as a pseudomagnetic field acting on normal matter. Such interactions can be modeled as usual magnetic interactions using spin-evolution (Bloch) equations. axionbloch, an open-source Python package for simulating spin dynamics induced by both usual and exotic interactions, is presented. The numerical simulations serve as a tool for deriving axion signal signatures, which are crucial for designing experimental searches and data analysis. Simulations are calibrated against theoretical expectations, ensuring the accuracy of the simulated signals. axionbloch is available at https://github.com/Yuzhe98/AxionBloch, allowing researchers to simulate pseudomagnetic signals under specific configurations of the axion models and experimental setups. The package is documented at http://axionbloch.readthedocs.io/ and includes example scripts for application.
item.dc:creator: Yuzhe Zhang

item.title: Dark Energy and Neutrino Flavor from the Weak Axion
item.description: arXiv:2607.13128v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dynamical dark energy offers an alternative to a cosmological constant with distinct observational signatures. However, the small energy density scale, Hubble-sized mass, and Planckian excursions make simple models fine-tuned and unnatural. In this work, we show that a weak version of the axion, identified with the phase field of the anomalous $U(1)_{B+L}$ of the Standard Model, can generate the scale hierarchies expected for dark energy. The axion potential is controlled by sources of explicit baryon and lepton number violation and is radiatively stable. We show that the leading contribution comes from two inequivalent Weinberg operators, one $B+L$-conserving and one $B+L$-violating, which generate the axion potential. We propose a flavor selection rule in the lepton sector that simultaneously removes the quadratic divergence and dominant temperature-dependent contributions to the effective potential. The resulting potential first appears at quartic order in the axion-dependent neutrino masses and, depending on the flavor model and PMNS parameters, its amplitude is parametrically close to the dark-energy density. Since the scale of dark energy is sensitive to changes in the neutrino parameters, improved measurements of $m_{\beta\beta}$, the sum of neutrino masses, $\delta_{\rm CP}$ and $\theta_{23}$ can favor certain models. Cosmologically, the field behaves as thawing quintessence, stays frozen by Hubble friction until late times and never enters the adiabatic regime.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Bittar, Carlos E. M. Wagner

item.title: A large size of the pion-like excitations in the stringy fluid above $T_{ch}$ is model independent and required by current algebra
item.description: arXiv:2608.04563v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multiple lattice evidences support the existence of a confining but chirally symmetric stringy fluid regime of QCD above the chiral symmetry restoration temperature at T_{ch} ~ 155 MeV. This regime is characterized by an approximate chiral spin symmetry and its extensions which means that the propagating excitations represent the chirally symmetric quarks connected into color singlets by the chromoelectric string. Clear \pi,\pi' peaks above T_{ch} were extracted on the lattice from the spatial and temporal correlators, which become broader with temperature and disappear roughly at $3T_{ch}$. The meson-like excitations above T_{ch} were studied within the manifestly confining and chirally symmetric model. It has been demonstrated that the chiral symmetry restoration in the confining regime happens because of Pauli blocking of the levels, required for the existence of the quark condensate, by the thermal quark excitation. The same Pauli blocking leads to a huge swelling of the low-spin mesons above T_{ch} which become infinitely large in the chiral limit. This property should be crucial for the explanation of the high collectivity and a very small mean-free path of the constituents above $T_{ch}$ seen experimentally. Here we demonstrate that the swelling of pions above T_{ch} is a model-independent effect required by current algebra.
item.dc:creator: L. Ya. Glozman

item.title: Isochrone fitting of Galactic globular clusters - IX. Tip of the red-giant branch for 27 clusters and constraints on new particle physics
item.description: arXiv:2608.04801v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Red-giant evolution is sensitive to non-standard channels of energy loss in stellar cores and therefore provides a probe of new physics. Such losses increase the luminosity of the tip of the red-giant branch (TRGB), the brightest point reached by a red giant in the color-magnitude diagram. Previous analyses of TRGB luminosities in globular clusters placed stringent bounds on the axion-electron coupling g_{ae}, but were limited by observational and theoretical uncertainties. To obtain a homogeneous and systematically controlled constraint, we use new parameters and TRGB estimates for 27 globular clusters, derived from Stetson, Hubble Space Telescope, and Gaia photometry, together with cluster-specific MESA calculations. Our primary likelihood uses 24 clusters after excluding three hot-flasher systems and explicitly accounts for stellar variability in identifying the brightest RGB stars. Finite sampling of the upper RGB is described by the full conditional distribution, and shared observational and stellar-physics uncertainties are retained as correlated nuisance parameters. The observed TRGB is fainter than the standard-cooling prediction by 0.078 (+0.036,-0.037) mag; to avoid an artificially strong bound from this downward fluctuation, we use the power-constrained profile likelihood method and obtain g_{ae}<6.4e-14 (95% CL). Sensitivity estimates for the neutrino magnetic dipole moment and for millicharged particles are also presented.
item.dc:creator: G. A. Gontcharov, A. M. Kudashov, O. S. Ryutina, S. V. Troitsky

item.title: Photon emission from rotating plasmas: a generalized McLerran-Toimela formula and the onset of superradiance
item.description: arXiv:2608.12098v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The photon emission and absorption spectra of a plasma rotating with constant angular velocity $\Omega$ are derived in terms of the spectral function of the current--current correlator. In contrast to the non-rotating case, the leading contribution arises already at one-loop order. The photon emission spectrum and its elliptic flow are calculated for a rotating quark--gluon plasma and compared with the leading two-loop result for a non-rotating plasma. The rotating plasma is found to emit significantly more soft photons than the non-rotating one. An analysis of the emission and absorption of cylindrical waves indicates that photons with energy $\omega$ and azimuthal quantum number $m$ satisfying $\omega<m\Omega$ are emitted at a higher rate than they are absorbed, thereby exhibiting the phenomenon of superradiance. It is further argued that these superradiant modes induce an instability of the magnetic field that is generated concurrently with the plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
item.dc:creator: Kirill Tuchin

item.title: Probing the Single Production of First-Generation Singlet Vector-like Leptons at Future $e^+e^-$ Colliders
item.description: arXiv:2608.14195v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the single production of first-generation weak-isosinglet vector-like leptons (VLLs) at future $e^+e^-$ colliders through $e^+e^-\to e^\pm E^\mp$, with the subsequent decays $E^\pm\to W^\pm\nu_e$, $e^\pm Z$, and $e^\pm h$. For the heavy VLL masses considered, the hadronic decays of the $W$ and $Z$ bosons are reconstructed as fat-jets, while the Higgs boson is reconstructed from two resolved $b$-tagged jets at $\sqrt{s}=1~{\rm TeV}$ and as a fat-jet at $\sqrt{s}=1.5~{\rm TeV}$. Using detector-level Monte Carlo simulations for the 1~TeV ILC and 1.5~TeV CLIC, we perform a baseline cut-based analysis in which the well-defined two-body production kinematics are exploited through a mass-hypothesis-dependent selection on the associated-electron energy. At fixed nominal center-of-mass energy, this observable is in one-to-one correspondence with the VLL recoil mass and therefore provides a common mass-sensitive discriminator for all three decay channels. We derive the $2\sigma$ exclusion and $5\sigma$ discovery reaches on the VLL--electron mixing angle $\sin\theta_L$ as functions of the integrated luminosity. For the benchmark points studied, sizeable sensitivity is retained at $m_E=900~{\rm GeV}$ at the ILC and $m_E=1400~{\rm GeV}$ at CLIC, while the accessible values of $\sin\theta_L$ extend below the reference electroweak precision bound used in this study. These results demonstrate the complementary potential of direct searches for first-generation singlet VLLs at future lepton colliders.
item.dc:creator: Yao-Bei Liu, Stefano Moretti

item.title: Triangle Feynman diagram in the timelike region
item.description: arXiv:2608.18894v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In Quantum Field Theory, triangle Feynman diagram $F(p_1^2,p_2^2,p_3^2|m_1,m_2,m_3)$ is an analytic function of its variables, whose analytic structure is fully determined by the location of singularities of the propagators of particles in the loop. The form factor $F(p_1^2,p_2^2,p_3^2|m_1,m_2,m_3)$ is easily calculable in the Euclidean region of all variables, $p_i^2<0$, $i=1,2,3$. A rigorous way to obtain the form factor in the timelike region is to perform the analytic continuation from the Euclidean region using single or double dispersion representations. On the other hand, there is a simple representation of the triangle as integral over Feynman parameters. We show that all known rigorous results of dispersion representations in the regions where some of the variables $p_i^2$ are in the physical Minkowski region, are reproduced by the Feynman-parameter representation for $F(p_1^2,p_2^2,p_3^2|m_1,m_2,m_3)$ through the extra replacements $p_i^2 \to p_i^2 + i0$ and $m_i^2 \to m_i^2 - i0$, where $m_i$ are masses of particles propagating in the loop. This implies that no deformation of the integration paths along the real axis of the Feynman parameters is forced by possible migrations of poles from the unphysical sheet to the physical one. The extra replacements allow us to take properly into account all subtle contributions given in the context of dispersion representations by the anomalous cuts and thresholds, and to provide the form factor on the upper boundaries of the cuts for all values of $p_i^2$.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail A. Ivanov, Dmitri Melikhov, Silvano Simula

item.title: Exploring a low-mass H dibaryon in light of the LZ event: A QCD sum rule study
item.description: arXiv:2610.25925v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Collaboration recently reported a candidate event consistent with a high-energy nuclear recoil, motivating a possible interpretation by Lee, Takahashi, and Tsai involving the production of an invisible baryon-number-two scalar with a mass near $1.85$ GeV. Motivated by this hypothetical scenario, we investigate the $J^P=0^+$ $uuddss$ hexaquark system using QCD sum rules. We consider five local diquark-diquark-diquark interpolating currents with different scalar and axial-vector diquark combinations, together with a baryon-baryon current constructed from two $\Lambda$-type baryon currents. The operator product expansions are calculated up to dimension sixteen, and their numerical behaviors are examined under different OPE truncations. Among the currents considered, only the $SU(3)_{\rm flavor}$-singlet current $J_{SSS}$, consisting of three scalar color-$\bar{\mathbf{3}}_C$ diquarks, yields a low-mass solution at $D=12$, with $M_{SSS}=1.85^{+0.19}_{-0.20}$ GeV. Interestingly, scalar color-$\bar{\mathbf{3}}_C$ diquarks belong to the flavor $\bar{\mathbf{3}}_F$ representation, and their local color-singlet construction has a unique nonvanishing flavor structure, $[ud][ds][su]$, corresponding to $uuddss$. Analogous all-scalar-diquark currents vanish for other flavor configurations, such as $uuuddd$ and $uuudds$. Together with our QCD sum-rule results, this property highlights the special role of the all-scalar-diquark configuration, $[ud][ds][su]$, as a possible deeply bound structure. However, the higher-dimensional OPE contributions exhibit significant truncation dependence, and the low-mass solution remains conditional on the adopted OPE truncation rather than constituting a fully controlled mass prediction.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Han Tan, Hua-Xing Chen

item.title: Understanding Big Bang Nucleosynthesis: the physics and its history
item.description: arXiv:2111.14254v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Big-bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) is a pillar of modern cosmology. It was the first major test of the hot big bang model, and today remains its earliest and most precise test. It all began with the trailblazing 1948 paper of Alpher, Bethe and Gamow, who proposed non-equilibrium nuclear processes in the early Universe and an early radiation-dominated phase to explain the abundances of all the chemical elements in the periodic table. While their neutron-capture model was deeply flawed, it initiated the path to the modern theory of BBN and the discovery of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). In this paper I clarify the basic physics of BBN, adding some new insights, and describe how the modern theory developed. I finish with a discussion of the pre-discovery predictions of the temperature of CMB, including the missteps and the missed opportunities. The legacy of big bang nucleosynthesis is enormous, and it is yet another illustration of how foggy it can be at the frontiers of discovery.
item.dc:creator: Michael S. Turner (KICP/UChicago,UCLA)

item.title: Periodic charge oscillations in the Proca theory
item.description: arXiv:2212.01951v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the Proca theory of the real massive vector field. There is a locally conserved 4-current operator in such a theory, which one may use to define the charge operator. Accordingly, there are charged states in which the expectation value of the charge operator is non-zero. We take a close look at the charge operator and study the dynamics of the certain class of charged states. For this purpose, we discuss the mean electric field and 4-current in such states. The mean electric field has the periodically oscillating Coulomb component, whose presence explains the periodic charge oscillations. A complementary insight at such a phenomenon is provided by the mean 4-current, whose discussion leads to the identification of a certain paradox. Last but not least, we show that there is a shock wave propagating in the studied system, which affects analyticity of the mean electric field and 4-current.
item.dc:creator: Bogdan Damski

item.title: Non-equilibrium dynamics of dipole-charged fields in the Proca theory
item.description: arXiv:2305.13908v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discuss the dynamics of field configurations encoded in the certain class of electric (magnetic) dipole-charged states in the Proca theory of the real massive vector field. We construct such states so as to ensure that the long distance structure of the mean electromagnetic field in them is initially set by the formula describing the electromagnetic field of the electric (magnetic) dipole. We analyze then how such a mean electromagnetic field evolves in time. We find that far away from the center of the initial field configuration, the long range component of the mean electromagnetic field harmonically oscillates, which leads to the phenomenon of the periodic oscillations of the electric (magnetic) dipole moment. We also find that near the center of the initial field configuration, the mean electromagnetic field escapes from its initial arrangement and a spherical shock wave propagating with the speed of light appears in the studied system. A curious configuration of the axisymmetric mean electric field is found to accompany the mean magnetic field in magnetic dipole-charged states.
item.dc:creator: Bogdan Damski

item.title: Examining the Anomalous Nature of Chiral Effects in Thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2507.02079v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum anomalies give rise to novel transport phenomena, including the generation of a current in a relativistic fluid due to the presence of magnetic field or vorticity. We present an exclusive and direct computation of the chiral anomaly in the adiabatic regime within the path integral for a massless fermion on a generic electromagnetic and curved background, including local temperature and chemical potential. We identify new quantum-thermodynamical contributions to the breaking of axial symmetry which induce the Chiral Separation and Vortical Effects.

item.title: Does hot QCD have a conformal manifold in the chiral limit?
item.description: arXiv:2603.09977v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent lattice evidence may suggest the chiral phase transition in QCD is second order for $N_f \ge 2$ massless flavors. We constrain conformal field theory (CFT) descriptions of a critical line in temperature $T$ and imaginary baryon chemical potential $\theta_B = i\mu_B/T$. An 't Hooft anomaly at general $\theta_B$ constrains the transition even at $\theta_B = 0$, leaving only three minimal scenarios. The best-motivated scenario for $N_f\ge3$, and perhaps also $N_f = 2$, is beyond Ginzburg-Landau, featuring a conformal manifold of $\theta_B$-dependent universality classes with an exactly marginal operator related to baryon density.

item.title: Remarks on MAMI's recent determination of $B_{\Lambda}({_{\Lambda}^3}{\rm H})$
item.description: arXiv:2604.18259v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A recent report on ${^7{\rm Li}}(e,e'K^+)$ electroproduction runs by the A1 collaboration at the Mainz Microtron (MAMI) assigns a sharp pion-momentum line at $p_{\pi^-}\approx 113.8\pm 0.1$ MeV/c to ${_{\Lambda}^3}{\rm H}\to\pi^-+{^3{\rm He}}$ weak decay, resulting in exceptionally large ${_{\Lambda}^3}{\rm H}$ binding-energy $B_{\Lambda}({_{\Lambda}^3}{\rm H})=0.523\pm 0.013\pm 0.075$ MeV. Here I discuss an alternative interpretation of the observed sharp line in terms of ${_{\Lambda}^7}{\rm He}_{\rm g.s.}\to\pi^-+{^7{\rm Li}}(E_{\rm x}=478$ keV) weak decay and its implications for $B_{\Lambda}({_{\Lambda}^7}{\rm He})$.

item.title: Search for Sub-GeV Axion-Like Particles at EBES Pilot Run Using 4 GeV Positron Beam at KEK LINAC
item.description: arXiv:2605.07108v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report the results of a search for sub-GeV axion-like particles (ALPs) using pilot run data from the Electron Beam-dump Experiment at KEK LINAC Switching Yard 3 (EBES). The data were collected in December 2023 with a 4 GeV positron beam and correspond to $5.7\times10^{13}$ positrons on target. In the pilot run setup, a tungsten beam dump and a single PbO calorimeter were used. We consider ALP production via the Primakoff process induced by bremsstrahlung photons in the beam dump, followed by the decay $a\to\gamma\gamma$. The background was estimated with a data-driven method, and a signal region was defined such that the expected background yield is below 0.1 events. No events were observed after unblinding. Upper limits at the 90% confidence level were derived in the ALP mass-coupling plane, extending the experimental coverage into a region of parameter space not explored by previous searches.

item.title: Linear causality and stability constraints on relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2606.00649v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we construct a theoretical framework for relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics based on entropy current analysis. The formalism consistently incorporates finite relaxation dynamics of the dissipative fluxes, providing a transient framework suitable for analyzing linear stability and short-wavelength causality. Utilizing linear mode analysis, we investigate the constraints imposed by causality and stability on this anisotropic system. By linearizing the theory around a homogeneous equilibrium state, we identify the magnetosonic, Alfv\'en, and charge-diffusion sectors, together with their coupling terms. For each sector, we derive asymptotic dispersion relations in both the long-wavelength (small-$k$) and short-wavelength (large-$k$) regimes, validating them against exact numerical roots. Our numerical analysis confirms the accuracy of these asymptotic solutions and uncovers a nontrivial angular dependence, especially near special propagation directions where the ordinary momentum expansion becomes less reliable. By evaluating the large-$k$ behavior of the propagating branches alongside the damping properties of non-hydrodynamic modes, we delineate the corresponding causality constraints. We find that the admissible linear causal domain is governed by the interplay between propagation direction, anisotropic transport coefficients, and relaxation times, with the resulting bounds being intrinsically mode-dependent. These findings provide a systematic theoretical basis for investigating linear stability and short-wavelength causality in relativistic magnetohydrodynamics beyond the first-order approximation.

item.title: Corrections induced by the GUP to the Lamb shift of an accelerated atom interacting with a quantum scalar field
item.description: arXiv:2608.26914v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the effect of the GUP on the Lamb shift of a two-level atom interacting with a real massless scalar quantum field, within the DDC formalism. For an atom undergoing inertial motion, uniform acceleration, and uniform circular motion, we analyze the separate contributions of vacuum fluctuations and radiation reaction. We first derive the statistical functions of the field along the atom's trajectories for the three types of motion, expressing them as frequency integrals, and then employ them to calculate the vacuum fluctuation and radiation reaction contributions to the radiative level shift. We show that the GUP-modified Lamb shift of the two-level atom arises entirely from vacuum fluctuations and acquires additional corrections proportional to $\beta$. We focus in particular on the acceleration-dependent GUP corrections. For a uniformly accelerated atom, the GUP corrections comprise thermal and nonthermal parts. At low accelerations, the thermal part exhibits nonmonotonic behavior, and is proportional to $a^4$ in the limit $a/\omega_0 \to 0$; the nonthermal part, by contrast, grows nonlinearly and monotonically, exceeding the thermal part by nearly two orders of magnitude at large accelerations. For an atom in uniform circular motion, the GUP corrections are purely nonthermal and also display a nonlinear, monotonic dependence on acceleration, increasing or decreasing steeply according to the sign of $\beta$. For the same $\beta$, the corrections are larger in uniform circular motion than in uniformly accelerated motion, since the former involves terms proportional to both $a^2$ and $a^3$, whereas the latter contains only $a^2$ terms.

item.title: A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe
item.description: arXiv:2610.24905v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a flat three-torus universe whose contraction is turned around by the negative Casimir energy of Standard Model fields. The trace anomaly forbids conformal matter alone to turn an anisotropic universe around, so matter with $w<1/3$, most cheaply a positive potential, must supply the negative trace; with antiperiodic fermions the Standard Model supplies the negative energy, and the universe turns at an edge of 722 reduced Planck lengths. The turning point can hold only about five quanta of the lowest modes, whereas a reheating coupling in a time-symmetric past would produce radiation exceeding the Casimir energy by at least $10^{94}$, so we read the turn as a beginning rather than a bounce. Negative Casimir energy cannot hold the shape of the torus: its shape state can be real at most once, and for a real Gaussian state survival of the shape on both branches with $90\%$ probability requires that moment to lie within $0.35$ Hubble times of the turn. The natural state, real at the turn, freezes the torus into a nearly rectangular box whose sides typically differ by $16$--$18\%$. The microwave background can read this fossil only if the shortest cycle lies between $0.985$ and about $1.04$ last-scattering diameters. At the turn the Higgs quartic coupling is negative, yet zero-point fluctuations of the gauge zero modes keep the Higgs zero mode near the origin with probability above one half for a top-quark pole mass below $172.96$ GeV, given a curvature coupling $\xi_H\gtrsim0.08$; a pole mass above $173.7$ GeV, within reach of FCC-ee, would exclude this beginning.
